## 1. Uninterrupted electricity supply was set to resume after a 270 MW coal unit returned to service.

The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">National System Operator</span> (the entity that runs the national grid) said scheduled demand management would cease, following restoration works at the plant. It announced the unit’s full load return at 1.31 p.m. and confirmed no further peak‑hour curtailment was required from October 22.

The move came days after an <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">islandwide outage on October 17</span>, when rooftop generators were asked to disconnect and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">one‑hour evening cuts</span> were implemented from October 19 to 21. Those rotations were published across four groups with 30‑minute restoration buffers, while investigations into the grid trip proceeded on a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">formal timetable</span>.

## 2. Draft anti‑terror and organised crime bills faced calls for withdrawal from legal professionals.

The Bar Association of Sri Lanka warned that proposed detention and bail provisions would weaken judicial oversight and risk curtailing liberties. It highlighted concerns about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">executive‑signed detention orders</span>, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">High Court‑only bail</span> for specified offences and broad definitions that could capture peaceful activity.

Separately, the Speaker reported that <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">40 petitions</span> had been filed against the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill (PSTA, a planned replacement for the PTA), with hearings held before a three‑judge bench. Earlier notices also listed dozens of petitions on the Sri Lanka Cricket Bill, indicating a heavy constitutional docket.

## 3. A yuan clearing facility was launched in Colombo to settle trade with China directly.

Authorised by the People’s Bank of China, the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Bank of China’s local branch</span> will act as the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">clearing bank</span> (a designated bank that settles payments between local banks and a foreign currency system) for cross‑border RMB transactions. The arrangement enables local banks to route payments without converting through US dollars, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">reducing currency conversion costs</span> and timing risk.

Officials from both countries attended the launch, which the Finance Ministry said would deepen financial links. The facility also seeks to streamline processing between local institutions and Chinese counterparts by providing a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">domestic settlement channel</span>.

## 4. Tea export volumes fell 2.9% in September as packet and bulk shipments slipped.

Customs data compiled by Forbes & Walker showed shipments at <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">23.09 million kilogrammes</span> versus 23.78 million a year earlier, while average <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">FOB value</span> (free‑on‑board, a price excluding freight and insurance) rose to US$ 5.85 per kg from US$ 5.76. Over January–September, volumes were <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">down 4.5% to 189.41 million kg</span> and average dollar values eased to US$ 5.73 per kg.

<span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Turkey led destinations</span> with purchases up 134% to 35.70 million kg, as Iraq dropped 39% to 18.43 million kg and Russia was broadly flat at 16.91 million kg. Tea bags and green tea secured higher dollar prices, while instant tea volumes grew 22.9% in the nine‑month period.

## 5. Prison population declined by 12% in the September quarter.

The Justice Minister told Parliament that inmate numbers <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">fell by 5,068</span> between July 1 and September 30 as bottlenecks eased, including faster Government Analyst reporting. The department issued <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">1,506 reports</span> in August and September after staffing was strengthened, and draft amendments would require reports <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">within two months</span> and allow court‑supervised <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">destruction of seized narcotics</span> based on photographic or video records.
